channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Brown Bear Population in Spain Doubles With Incredible Increase of its Breeding Range
item.description: Cantabrian brown bears have doubled to about 370 in 20 years and now range across 6,500 square miles. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 100-Year-Old ‘Store Mom’ Surprised With Her First Birthday Party
item.description: Store staff threw a first-ever surprise party for a 100-year-old who walks their aisles every day. How you can help: Learn the name of someone you see every day and ask how they are. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘There’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the Closet’ – Words that Led to Painting’s Joyous Rediscovery
item.description: A Georgia O'Keeffe painting kept for years in a family closet has been found and identified. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Brave Teens Execute Paddleboard Rescue of Flooded Neighbors – ‘Faith in Humanity Restored’
item.description: Teenagers paddled through floodwater to bring a stranded mother and son to safety when crews could not reach them. How you can help: Check on neighbours when a flood warning is issued, especially anyone living alone. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
item.description: Experiments suggest Earth made its own water as hot rock reacted with hydrogen, rather than receiving it from comets. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A campaign to save one tree in Aachen grew into moss walls that cool and clean city air. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Historic US ocean liner sinks near Florida to become world’s largest artificial reef
item.description: The liner SS United States has been sunk off Destin to become the world's largest artificial reef. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: After a decade of community pressure, LA bans oil drilling for good
item.description: After more than ten years of pressure from residents living beside wells, Los Angeles has banned oil drilling. Evidence: Now policy. How you can help: Go to a council meeting on a local planning issue; steady turnout is what moved this. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: For Centuries, Visitors Walked Right by 280 Unseen Ice Age Cave Paintings
item.description: About 280 Ice Age engravings were found in a Spanish cave that visitors had walked past for centuries. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘I pulled him out, I heard more screaming’ – How a Cadet Saved a Father and Son from Drowning
item.description: A merchant marine cadet pulled a father and his son from a swimming pool and both survived. How you can help: Take a basic rescue and CPR course; pools and first aid groups run them often. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved
item.description: Hair follicle patterns arise from cells following chemical signals, a simpler process than long believed. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Paralysis Could Not Stop Her: How This 84-year-old Made Good on Her Musical Promise
item.description: An 84-year-old who recovered from paralysis now plays piano for residents of the home that treated her. How you can help: Ask a care home near you whether it welcomes volunteer musicians or visitors. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Bid to restore rare Atlantic rainforest secures £6m lottery grant
item.description: A £6m grant will fund hubs training people to restore rare Atlantic rainforest in the West Highlands. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Join a woodland restoration day near you; most groups provide tools and training. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
item.description: Each mosquito species turns out to follow its own mix of skin odours, a lead for better targeted repellents. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
item.description: Fossils of a 66-pound rodent from Thailand show giant rodents evolved far earlier than thought. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
item.description: A 237-million-year-old armoured amphibian found in China appears to have lived in the sea. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Prince Bashangezi turned personal loss into peer tutoring for refugee students
item.description: Prince Bashangezi started peer tutoring for refugee students after schools closed, and it is still running. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Offer an hour a week of tutoring through a school or library near you. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Brazil releases the world’s first fossil fuel phaseout roadmap
item.description: Brazil has published a national roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels, the first country to set one out. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
item.description: A new way of cleaning James Webb images revealed a planet that had been hidden in existing data. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ‘Nothing short of a miracle’ – Rescuers Find Boy with Autism Missing for 3 Days
item.description: A six-year-old autistic boy missing for three days was found safe by a volunteer searcher on a horse trail. How you can help: Ask your local search and rescue team how volunteers can train and join. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Jimmy Carter’s Georgia farm acquired by conservation group planning to open it to public
item.description: A conservation group has bought Jimmy Carter's family farm to protect the land and open it to the public. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: A Viral Video Led Strangers to Raise $76,000 for a Full-Time Caregiver
item.description: Strangers who saw a doorbell video gave more than $76,000 to a woman who spends her days caring for others. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World’s Driest Desert Erupts into Record-Breaking Bloom Boom (LOOK)
item.description: Rare rain has brought some 200 plant species into flower across Chile's Atacama, the largest bloom recorded there. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
item.description: A 450-million-year-old starfish relative was found with its soft tissue preserved, a very rare survival. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
item.description: Four volunteers have walked out healthy after more than a year living in NASA's simulated Mars habitat. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
item.description: After a 40-year search, CERN has evidence of a particle decay that happens about once in 10 billion. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Electric ferries that fly above water are arriving in the US
item.description: Electric hydrofoil ferries that ride above the water and use far less energy are starting service in US cities. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
item.description: Scientists traced a gut-to-brain dopamine pathway that explains how people come to enjoy bitter tastes like coffee. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Man’s Halloween Skeletons Prove Perfect Treat to Woman Battling Breast Cancer
item.description: A yard full of Halloween skeletons became the bright spot on one woman's weekly drive to cancer treatment. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding play corners, childcare help and flexible advising so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: If you study or teach, ask what your college offers student parents and pass it on. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Interpreting Autistic Cues Is Difficult, a Teen Built an App That’s Helping Hundreds of Families
item.description: A teenager built an app that helps families read autistic cues; over 700 people in 12 countries now use it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Fish Stocks Thrive Thanks to This Pink Seaweed and Locals Who Protected It
item.description: Ten years after islanders won a scallop dredging ban, the pink maerl seabed and its fish stocks are thriving. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Choose hand-dived or creel-caught shellfish over dredged when you have the choice. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Glowworms Shine Again in the UK from Larvae Reared Pro Bono in Garden Shed
item.description: Glowworms are lighting up UK sites again, bred from larvae a volunteer rears in his garden shed. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Leave a corner of the garden unlit and unmown; glowworms need dark, rough grass. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
item.description: A UCLA study suggests a naturally occurring molecule may ease the brain fog that lingers after breast cancer treatment. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
item.description: NASA has set out a faster plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with an orbital test in 2027. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
item.description: Stickier ocean "marine snow" carries up to six times more carbon to the deep sea, sharpening climate models. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
item.description: A fossil site in Colombia preserves a whole ancient sea community of giant reptiles and sharks. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dogs Can Sniff-Out Invasive Plant Species With High Accuracy to Curb Their Destruction
item.description: Volunteer pet dogs in Germany learned to sniff out invasive plants accurately, so they can be removed early. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: At a Montana guest ranch, autistic people work as wranglers, guides, cooks and concierges. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Choose stays and services from businesses that employ autistic staff. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: The Student Exchange Program That Never Leaves the U.S.
item.description: A student exchange sends American teenagers to live with families in very different parts of their own country. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding purpose and community by taking up small-scale farming. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants to safety so its Victorian Palm House can be restored for the future. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer
item.description: A fossil collected in Antarctica in 1985 and left in a drawer turns out to be a Titanosaur tail bone. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
